n1.text: Does the boiler shut off on a high-limit or high supply temperature, rather than when the setpoint is satisfied?

options.label: Yes, high limit or high temperature

n2.text: Is there good flow while the boiler runs (pump running, valves open, strainer clean)?

r_flow.cause: Insufficient flow is overheating the boiler.
fix: Check the pump, isolation and zone valves, strainer and air.
Confirm the boiler's minimum flow requirement in its manual.
Do not raise or bypass the high limit.

n2b.text: Is the supply setpoint or reset curve higher than the building load needs?

r_setpt.cause: The setpoint is too high for the load, so the boiler reaches it quickly and shuts off.
fix: Lower the setpoint or reset curve (Readings tab for a check).
Review differential and minimum-on-time settings in the control manual.
Consider the manufacturer's guidance on minimum load or buffer volume.
Check supply sensor accuracy against a calibrated thermometer and check its wiring.
Review control differential and anti-cycle settings per the manual.
Record any codes and look them up in the Fault codes tab.

n3.text: Does it shut off because the call for heat ends (zone or thermostat satisfied quickly)?

options.label: No, it stops with the call still present

n4.text: Is the heating load small compared with the boiler's minimum output (few zones calling)?

r_oversize.cause: Boiler minimum output exceeds the load for the zones currently calling.
fix: Check modulation and minimum-fire settings per the manual.
Consider buffer volume or zoning changes as recommended by the manufacturer.
Check thermostat cycle-rate and anticipator settings and its location.
Check for zone valve end-switch chatter.
Check for a thermostat or sensor drifting or reading a draft.

r_interlock.cause: Cycling is caused by a safety or sensor interlock opening.
fix: Check flame signal, air or flue pressure switch, flow switch and low-water cut-off status per the manual.
Record any codes and look them up in the Fault codes tab.
Do not bypass any safety interlock.
